correctness.rationale: Fix the source recurrence (1/d)Σ_facets[facet (d−1)-volume / orthogonal central-section (d−1)-volume] W_{d−1}(section), and W1=2. The section of the 4-cross-polytope by Σx_i=0 is the 12-vertex cuboctahedron C=conv{(e_i−e_j)/2:i≠j}, ordinary 3-volume 5/6. Its eight equilateral triangular facets each have area √3/8, orthogonal section regular hexagon of area 3√3/4 and W2=3; six square facets have area 1/2, square central section area 1 and W2=4. The contributions to 3W3(C) are 4 and 12, so W3(C)=16/3. The sixteen tetrahedron facets of B each have Euclidean 3-volume 1/3 and section C volume 5/6, so W4(B)=16·(1/4)·(1/3)·(16/3)/(5/6)=128/15. The four-cube polar has coordinate facets parallel to equal-volume central cubical sections and W4=16 by recursion. Exact independent rational cancellation confirms 8/15; all facet counts and geometry are given explicitly, and numerical hull code is corroboration, not a proof of a global property.
